summary: This article explains how the Amazon River forms where the Solimões meets the Rio Negro, carries more water than any other river on Earth, floods its forest every year, and shapes life for the villages along its banks.
introduce: Read the title “The Amazon River” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: the amount of water that flows out of a river in a certain amount of time
all of the land that drains its rain and streams into one river
sand, mud, and tiny bits of rock carried along by moving water

challengeTerms.def: deep or wide enough for boats to travel on safely
an area of land where all the water drains toward the same river or lake
how tightly packed the mass of a substance is, which affects whether it floats, sinks, or stays separate from another substance

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that living in a village that can only be reached by boat would be more fun than living in a town with roads? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two reasons the Amazon carries so much more water than most other rivers.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review discharge, basin, and sediment, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use navigable, watershed, and density in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
